subject.title: [Bug]: doctor last-known-good restore never converges when the restored legacy config fails its own migration; manual live-file fixes get reverted

question: When a last-known-good snapshot cannot survive current doctor migrations and validation, should doctor fail without restoring it, or should it persist a separately migrated-and-validated replacement only after that candidate proves convergent?
rationale: Both choices change the recovery contract for invalid live configurations; the safe implementation boundary depends on whether automatic restoration may ever replace an operator-edited live file after a failed candidate migration.

options.title: Preflight the candidate before restore
options.body: Migrate and validate the snapshot in memory, then overwrite the live file only when the resulting canonical configuration can be persisted.

options.title: Fail without restoring
options.body: Keep the live file untouched when the snapshot is incompatible and report that both the live candidate and recovery snapshot require manual repair.

recommendation.title: Preflight the candidate before restore
recommendation.body: Migrate and validate the snapshot in memory, then overwrite the live file only when the resulting canonical configuration can be persisted.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter has the most complete observed incident and source-trace context available in this review; code-history ownership should be added after an exact-head provenance pass.
